title: Exception Safety and Invariant Incompletion
platform_conditions: C++11 and later on any conforming toolchain; noexcept violation calls std::terminate per the standard
security_mechanism: An exception unwinds a constructor or mutator midway, leaving the object half-updated: members assigned before the throw keep new values while later invariants (an initialized lock, a registered resource) are missing, and any code that catches and continues now operates on an object whose advertised class invariant is false. Declaring a function noexcept and throwing anyway calls std::terminate, aborting the process from inside what should be a recoverable path — a request-reachable crash. Destructors must not let exceptions escape because unwinding already in progress makes a second throw terminate the program.

source_sink_clues.source: Any operation that can fail at runtime under attacker influence: bad allocations under request load, parse failures on malformed input, IO errors — each raising while an object is mid-mutation.
source_sink_clues.sink: Throwing destructors or noexcept functions that throw; multi-step mutation sequences without rollback (no RAII guard) whose early steps persist when a later step throws

tracking_guards: Check that destructors are noexcept and swallow or log rather than rethrow, that throwing functions are not marked noexcept, and that multi-step mutations use RAII transaction guards or copy-and-swap so the object is either fully updated or untouched (strong exception guarantee).
not_candidate_when: The mutating operations are marked noexcept (no unwind can interrupt them), the state is rebuilt from scratch on the error path so no half-state survives, or the exception path exits the process before the object is used again.
